1. Every route under web/src/app (URL pattern → what the page shows, key interactive elements: buttons, drag lists, accept/reject, detail panels, settings/weights sliders, AI prompt for weights, profiles, generations, decision memory, social/concept test).
2. Where market/series data lives (files, shape of feature requests, profiles, sources, weights), which markets exist (europe/china/usa?) and series, and whether China/USA data exists and how much. Name exact file paths and the TypeScript types/fields a new data set must fill.
3. Whether any data is fetched from a backend/API (web/src/app/api) vs static modules, and whether any LLM call happens live (which env keys needed).
4. How to run it locally (package.json scripts, port).
5. Any existing image assets of cars/profiles (web/public) and how profile images are referenced.
Do not modify files.

| User intent | Tool | Triggers (any of) |
|---|---|---|
| **Try on / add / replace any wearable item (clothing, hats, sunglasses, shoes, accessories)** | `vto` | "try on", "what would I look like in", "dress me in", "put X on me / on the model", "add these sunglasses", "replace the hat/pants with this one", "swap X for this reference", "virtual try-on", "see me wearing", any brand + wearable ("Nike hoodie", "red dress") combined with a personal image |
| **More versions of a specific past result** | `generate_variations` | "more like that", "another version of this one", "variations of [request_id]" |
| **Any video / clip / animation** | `generate_video` | "make a video", "animate this (image)", "clip", "footage", "transition / morph between these images", "continue / extend this video", "smooth transition between keyframes" |
| **Full-quality render of a DRAFT video made in this chat** | `enhance_video` | "make this draft full quality", "finalize the draft", "render the draft I picked" — every trigger requires a draft from `generate_video(draft: true)`; nothing else routes here |
| **Change what is IN a finished video** | `edit_video` | "remove the X from this video", "replace the sign", "make it look like 16mm film", "turn day into night", "change her jacket to red", "edit this video" |
| **Make a finished video sharper / bigger** | `upscale_video` | "upscale this", "make it 4K", "higher resolution", "sharper", "clean this clip up" |
| **Everything else (T2I, edits, inpainting, style transfer, multi-reference, object swap)** | `generate_image` | every other prompt |

If the user's message contains a try-on intent — even subtly, e.g. "I want to try red Nike sportswear" or "what do I look like in this jacket" — `vto` is the right tool. "Try-on" is broader than clothing: adding or swapping ANY wearable item (hat, sunglasses, glasses, shoes, bag, jewelry) using a reference image of that item is a try-on, and so is replacing one worn item with another ("replace her hat with this one"). The subject doesn't have to be human — dressing a pet or mascot in a garment still routes to `vto`; don't switch back to `generate_image` mid-flow because the subject is an animal. Do NOT default to `generate_image` and describe the item in prose; the try-on endpoint preserves face and pose much better than prompt-only edits (which visibly alter faces). See the **Virtual Try-On** section below for the full flow (it includes a web-search step for sourcing brand garments).

## Video mode selection (`generate_video`)

`generate_video` takes a `requests` array (up to 4 entries, each one video — batch multi-video asks into ONE call, like `generate_image`). Each entry picks an explicit `mode`, and user-provided media MUST go in the matching mode's field — NEVER describe provided media in prose and call with `t2v` (the model invents everything from scratch and the result will look unrelated to the user's media):

| User intent | Mode + fields |
|---|---|
| Text only, no media | `mode: "t2v"` |
| Animate a single image / bring this picture to life | `mode: "i2v"`, `keyframes: [{image}]` |
| Transition / morph / interpolate BETWEEN two images | `mode: "i2v"`, `keyframes: [{image}, {image}]` (first = opening frame, second = closing frame) |
| Storyboard through 3-10 images | `mode: "i2v"`, one keyframe per image + explicit `duration` — or per-keyframe `timestamp` (seconds, all-or-none) to pin exact positions; with timestamps `duration: "auto"` runs the clip to the last timestamp |
| Continue / extend an existing clip | `mode: "v2v"`, `start_video` (chain calls to go past 20s) |

content.text:
Dixi has no data backend. All market and series data comes from static modules plus one local JSON file, and decisions, generations and settings are saved in the browser's localStorage. Only one feature makes a live AI call. China has no customer feedback at all.

**1. Routes** (pages in `/Volumes/PJ/peresjav/hackathons/ehl-final-minuch-2026/web/src/app`)
- `/`: landing page with Hero (3D market globe with sample comment bubbles), Process, Cars (photo strip) and Product (mock screenshot).
- `/dashboard`: a list of saved generations with KPI tiles (`DashboardHome tab="generations"`).
- `/dashboard/new`: starts a new analysis with a market picker on the globe (`MarketPicker`).
- `/dashboard/[market]`: `market` is `eu|cn|us|jp|all`. It shows `SeriesPicker` with the 1, 5 and 7 Series.
- `/dashboard/[market]/[series]`: `series` is `1-series|5-series|7-series`. This is the main demo screen (`components/pipeline/Pipeline.tsx`):
  - A car banner and the series principles.
  - A request list you drag to set priority, with flame icons for urgency and a reset button.
  - Keep / Reject on each request. Reject opens `RejectDialog`, which requires a reason.
  - A detail panel per request: quotes, sources, an option-list match, customer-study scores.
  - `SignalsPanel`: competitor and trend signals you can add to a wishlist.
  - A "Build profiles" button. It creates three profiles (fix / tech / comfort), each with an L1/L2/L3 score, and saves a generation.
  - `Analytics`: "Test the profiles on social media". It shows AI-made post images and 14-day engagement curves. These curves are simulated and always come out the same for the same inputs.
  - `DecisionLog`: the decision memory.
- `/dashboard/generations#<id>`: reopens a saved generation (`GenerationView`).
- `/dashboard/settings`: "Scoring and decision memory".
  - Weights: wDemand, wBacking, wFit.
  - Memory controls: rejectPenalty, keepBonus, halfLifeDays, resurfaceAt, hideRejected, memoryScope.
  - `WeightsAssistant`: a plain-language prompt that proposes new settings. You review and apply them, and changes are logged.

**2. Data**
- The types are in `web/src/lib/pipeline/types.ts`:
  - `PipelineData {origin, generatedAt, series[]}`
  - `SeriesData {id, name, feedbackByMarket, requests, strengths, studies, sales, options}`
  - `FeatureRequest {id, series, title, category, summary, mentions, byMarket, types, sources, quotes, taxonomy, relatedOptions}`
  - `MarketSignal {id, kind, series[], markets, title, competitor?, category, detail, relatesTo (exact request titles), strength, sources}`
- `SeriesId` is fixed to `"F70" | "G60" | "G70"`. `Category` is Exterior, Interior, Digital or Powertrain. `MarketId` is EU, CN, US or JP (`lib/markets.ts`), and feedback data can also use `"OTHER"`.
- Where the data comes from:
  - `web/data-local/pipeline.json`: 162 KB, origin "bmw", git-ignored, built by `scripts/build-pipeline-data.py`.
  - If that file is missing, `lib/pipeline/example.ts` is used instead (made-up data). The loader is `lib/pipeline/load.ts`.
  - Per-series settings (principles, competitors, l3Weight, focus) are in `lib/pipeline/series.ts`.
  - 32 market signals are in `lib/pipeline/market-signals.ts` (12 tagged CN, 15 tagged US).
  - Profile archetypes and scoring logic are in `lib/pipeline/profiles.ts` and `scoring.ts`.
  - Globe sample comments are in `lib/markets.ts` and are illustrative only.
- Coverage in the local file (25 requests per series):

| Series | Feedback records | Requests by market | Studies | Sales |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F70 (1 Series) | EU 1433, JP 672, OTHER 23 | EU 25, JP 25 | EU only | CN and US are 0 |
| G60 (5 Series) | US 3610, EU 111, JP 53, OTHER 226 | US 25, EU 20 | CN, EU, US | all markets |
| G70 (7 Series) | US 3792, EU 19, JP 40, OTHER 149 | US 25, EU 14 | CN, EU, US | all markets |

- **China has no feedback records in any series.** When a market has zero volume, `Pipeline.tsx:92` falls back to all-market mention counts.
- **The USA has no data for the 1 Series.**
- New data must fill `SeriesData` and `FeatureRequest` with exactly these fields. Adding a new series also means widening the `SeriesId` union and adding entries to `series.ts` and `car-images.ts`.

**3. Backend and AI**
- The only API route is `POST /api/scoring-advice` (`src/app/api/scoring-advice/route.ts`), called by `WeightsAssistant`.
- It makes the only live AI call, to OpenAI chat completions. It needs `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the environment or from the repo-root `../.env`. `OPENAI_MODEL_FAST` is optional; without it the route tries `gpt-6-luna`, then `gpt-5-mini`, then `gpt-4.1-mini`.
- Without a key it falls back to keyword rules (`adviseByRules`), so the feature still works on camera.
- `.env.example` lists API_URL and Supabase variables, but nothing in `src` reads them.

**4. Running it**
Run `pnpm install`, then `pnpm dev` and open http://localhost:3000 (the default port). Other scripts are `pnpm build`, `pnpm start` and `pnpm lint`. Next.js is 16.4.0.

**5. Images** (in `web/public/images`)
- Car photos in `cars/`: `f70-front`, `f70-rear`, `g60-front`, `g60-interior`, `g70-front`, `g70-rear` (`.webp`). They are Wikimedia CC BY-SA, with JSON sidecars, and are referenced from `src/lib/car-images.ts` (`CAR_IMAGES[id].front/second`). The licence needs the credit shown next to each image.
- Profile post images in `posts/`: `{f70,g60,g70}-{fix,tech,comfort}.webp`. They are AI-generated, with prompts in `scripts/prompts/posts.json`, and referenced in `lib/pipeline/posts.ts:54` as `/images/posts/${series}-${profileId}.webp`.
- Also `layers-abstract.png` and `product-dashboard.png`. There are no people or avatar images.

**Demo tips**
- Use `/dashboard/eu/1-series` or `/dashboard/us/5-series` for real data. `cn` will show fallback data.
- To start clean, clear the localStorage keys (`dixi:sessions`, plus the decision, scoring and user keys).
